title: Organisational Culture
summary: Organisational culture = 成员在共同经历中学到的共享知识、价值、信念与假设，影响什么被视为适当的工作方式（Schein & Schein 2017）
Schein 三层：Artifacts（布局、衣着、语言、会议）→ Espoused beliefs and values（使命、政策中宣称的）→ Basic underlying assumptions（习以为常、未经讨论）；容易观察 ≠ 容易解释
Stated values vs practised values：看优先级冲突时怎样决定、谁被认可、什么行为被纠正；有差距也不能直接断定全员虚伪；组织内存在 subcultures
Built to Last（Collins & Porras 1994）：18 家远见型公司 vs 18 家对照公司的历史比较，不是永久成功公式
四误区：①不必始于绝妙产品（Sony 电饭煲失败）②clock building > time telling（不依赖魅力领导）③利润可与更广宗旨并存，core ideology = core values + broader purpose ④preserve the core, stimulate progress（保留核心、更新做法）
Culture strength = consensus（共享广度）+ intensity（认同与社会强化程度）（Chatman & O'Reilly 2016）；strength ≠ content，强文化不是自动的赞美
Sørensen (2002)：强文化在稳定环境中与更可靠（一致稳定）的绩效相关，波动环境中该优势消失；可靠 ≠ 高利润，优势消失 ≠ 必然下降
五种可见形式（Trice & Beyer 1984）：rituals（Walmart cheer）、slogans（Nike Just Do It）、ceremonies（公开表彰）、heroes（榜样故事）、symbols（Nordstrom 倒金字塔）；可重叠，均需核查实践
Hofstede 六维度：power distance、individualism/collectivism、uncertainty avoidance、masculinity/femininity、long/short-term orientation、indulgence/restraint——国家层面倾向，不等于个人行为或组织文化
Independent self（个人属性与偏好）vs interdependent self（关系、角色、相互依存）（Markus & Kitayama 1991）；人可随情境表现两种取向
Cultural mismatch：制度期待与成员价值不符；Stephens et al. (2012)：美国大学强调独立的规范与部分第一代大学生（父母未上大学）的互依取向错配 → 不适、任务更难、表现较差；差异 ≠ 能力不足
Inclusive culture：recognise differences、create opportunities for participation、align practices with inclusive values
Competing Values Framework（Quinn & Rohrbaugh 1983）：Clan/Involvement（内部+灵活）、Adhocracy/Adaptability（外部+灵活）、Hierarchy/Consistency（内部+稳定控制）、Market/Achievement（外部+稳定控制）；没有普遍最优
Values–performance matrix：目标达成 × 价值践行两维分开诊断；管理文化四步 diagnose → clarify → align → evaluate

concepts.def: Shared knowledge, values, beliefs and assumptions that members learn through common experience, shaping what they see as appropriate ways of working.
concepts.defZh: 群体在应对外部要求和内部关系时学到的，成功做法逐渐被视为理所当然（Schein & Schein 2017）。
concepts.one: 组织文化是成员共同学到的价值、信念和假设，决定大家觉得怎样做才合适。
concepts.eg: 团队一直表扬主动帮同事的人，新人慢慢就学会了：遇到困难要去找人合作。
concepts.like: 像一群人长期同行后形成的走路习惯，没人写下却人人照做。

concepts.def: Visible features of culture such as layout, dress, language, meetings and everyday behaviour.
concepts.defZh: Schein 第一层；容易观察但不容易解释，例如开放式办公室不证明成员敢提异议。
concepts.one: 可见表征是文化看得见的表层，比如办公布局和会议，好观察但难解读。
concepts.eg: 公司有开放式办公室，每月还开全员大会，但这证明不了员工真的敢提反对意见。
concepts.like: 像冰山露出水面的尖角，看得见，却说明不了水下的形状。

concepts.def: What the organisation formally states is important, e.g. in mission statements, policies and management messages.
concepts.defZh: Schein 第二层；需与践行价值（实际决策、认可、被接受的行为）对照。
concepts.one: 宣称的价值是组织公开说重要的东西，比如使命和政策，要对照实际做法检验。
concepts.eg: 公司官网写着重视员工福祉，却一次次拒绝处理过重的工作量，说一套做一套。
concepts.like: 像菜单上写着「清淡」，要尝过端上来的菜才知道真假。

concepts.def: Taken-for-granted beliefs that shape action without conscious discussion.
concepts.defZh: Schein 最深层，例如默认质疑经理会伤害职业发展。
concepts.one: 基本假设是文化最深的一层：大家习以为常、不再讨论，却在暗中支配行动。
concepts.eg: 公司嘴上说开放，员工却私下默认：质疑经理会影响自己的前途，所以都不说话。
concepts.like: 像水面下的冰山主体，看不见，却决定船会不会撞上。

concepts.def: Different patterns of expectations that develop across teams, occupations or locations within an organisation.
concepts.defZh: 不能从一个部门或一位员工推出整个组织文化一致。
concepts.one: 亚文化是同一组织里不同团队、职业或地点各自形成的一套期待。
concepts.eg: 同一家公司里，研发部门习惯先动手试验，运营部门则习惯先把流程核对一遍。
concepts.like: 像同一支乐队的不同声部，各有惯例，但合奏的是同一首曲子。

concepts.def: Building lasting organisational capabilities (roles, routines, succession, shared values) rather than relying on one charismatic leader.
concepts.defZh: Built to Last 误区二；魅力有帮助但不等于建设耐久组织。
concepts.one: 造钟是建立不靠某个人的程序、接班安排和共享价值，报时是只靠魅力领导。
concepts.eg: 创始人事事亲自拍板，没培养接班人，他一退休公司就陷入困境，这就是只会报时。
concepts.like: 像报时人只能说出此刻几点，造钟人留下他不在也能走的钟。

concepts.def: Core values plus a broader purpose beyond making money.
concepts.defZh: 误区三；例子：HP 技术贡献、Nordstrom 顾客服务、Merck 药品与患者宗旨；利润仍重要。
concepts.one: 核心理念是核心价值加上赚钱之外的更大目的；利润重要，但不是唯一宗旨。
concepts.eg: Nordstrom 以顾客服务为核心，Merck 以药品服务患者为宗旨，但两家都要盈利。
concepts.like: 像开船：燃料（利润）必不可少，但航行是为了去某个目的地。

concepts.def: Keeping key commitments while changing how the organisation operates.
concepts.defZh: 误区四；不是保护每个熟悉惯例，例：大学保持高质量教育宗旨但改为线上/混合教学。
concepts.one: 守住真正核心的承诺，同时大胆更新具体做法；不是把所有老习惯都保护起来。
concepts.eg: 大学坚持高质量教育这个宗旨不变，但把面授改成线上或混合教学，考核方式也更新了。
concepts.like: 像一家人搬了新家、换了家具，但家规和感情不变。

concepts.def: How widely expectations are shared (consensus) and how strongly they are held and reinforced (intensity).
concepts.defZh: Chatman & O'Reilly（2016）；不是人数、标语音量或经理意志。
concepts.one: 文化强度看两点：多少人共享这些期待（共识），大家坚持得多坚定（强度）。
concepts.eg: 团队里几乎人人都认同提交前要核查质量，而且还会互相提醒必须照做。
concepts.like: 像一条班规：全班都认可、还会互相监督，才算真正立住。

concepts.def: What values and behaviours members actually support.
concepts.defZh: 与强度分开评价；强文化不保证内容合适、合乎伦理或绩效更高。
concepts.one: 文化内容是文化具体鼓励什么行为，要和强度分开看：强文化不等于好文化。
concepts.eg: 两家公司都高度一致：一家坚定鼓励试验新方法，另一家坚定要求严守流程。
concepts.like: 像两支纪律同样严明的球队，一支专练进攻，一支专练防守。

concepts.def: Strong cultures were associated with more reliable performance in relatively stable environments, but this advantage disappeared in volatile environments.
concepts.defZh: 可靠 = 一致稳定，不是利润最高；是关联不是因果定律。
concepts.one: 强文化在稳定环境里让绩效更可靠，但环境一旦多变，这个优势就消失了。
concepts.eg: 一家强文化公司在稳定市场里交付一直很可靠，市场骤变后表现就开始起伏了。
concepts.like: 像走熟路：路况稳定时总能准时，路况骤变时熟路未必还管用。

concepts.def: A repeated activity in which members participate and express shared meaning.
concepts.defZh: 例：Walmart cheer；重复动作本身不足以证明共享意义。
concepts.one: 仪式是成员反复参与、借此表达共同意义的活动。
concepts.eg: Walmart 的员工反复一起喊口号，拼出公司名称，并强调顾客第一。
concepts.like: 像球队赛前的固定呼喊，把共同身份一遍遍带进日常。

concepts.def: A planned event that publicly marks an occasion or achievement, communicating which contributions the organisation values.
concepts.defZh: 与 ritual 区别：庆典强调公开标记事件/成就，ritual 强调重复参与；两者可重叠。
concepts.one: 庆典是有计划地公开标记某个事件或成就，告诉大家组织看重哪种贡献。
concepts.eg: 公司在年度活动上公开表彰跨部门协作的团队，让大家知道这种合作受重视。
concepts.like: 像颁奖台：把值得学习的表现举起来给所有人看。

concepts.def: Heroes are people presented as models of valued behaviour; symbols are objects, actions or images that carry cultural meaning.
concepts.defZh: 例：Nordstrom 倒金字塔（顾客在顶、管理层在下）；需核查一线是否真有权限与资源。
concepts.one: 英雄是被当作榜样讲述的人物，象征物是带有文化意义的物件、动作或图像。
concepts.eg: Nordstrom 的倒金字塔把顾客放最上、管理层放最下，表达的是支持一线服务。
concepts.like: 像故事里的主角和队徽：一个供人模仿，一个代表认同。

concepts.def: Power distance, individualism/collectivism, uncertainty avoidance, masculinity/femininity, long/short-term orientation, indulgence/restraint.
concepts.defZh: 描述国家层面广泛倾向；national culture ≠ individual behaviour ≠ organisational culture。
concepts.one: 六个维度描述的是国家层面的大体文化倾向，不能直接套到某个人或某家公司。
concepts.eg: 得知成员来自高不确定性规避的国家，经理先问他们需要哪些规则，而不是默认人人爱严格流程。
concepts.like: 像一个城市的平均气温：说明大体气候，却定不了每个人穿什么。

concepts.def: Independent self emphasises personal attributes and preferences; interdependent self emphasises relationships, roles, belonging and mutual dependence.
concepts.defZh: Markus & Kitayama（1991）；个人可随情境表现两种，不能凭国籍或阶层贴标签。
concepts.one: 独立自我看重个人的特点和偏好，互依自我看重关系、角色和彼此依存。
concepts.eg: 团队自我介绍时，一个人先讲自己的专长和兴趣，另一个人先讲自己在团队里的角色。
concepts.like: 像介绍自己时先说「我擅长什么」，还是先说「我是谁的队友」。

concepts.def: When institutional or organisational expectations do not match the values and motives that members bring.
concepts.defZh: Stephens 等（2012）美国大学研究：独立规范与部分第一代大学生互依取向错配；差异 ≠ 错配 ≠ 能力不足。
concepts.one: 组织默认的期待和成员的价值观不合拍，让人不适、更吃力，但不代表能力差。
concepts.eg: Stephens 等（2012）：美国大学推崇独立，互依的第一代大学生感到不适、表现较差。
concepts.like: 像左撇子用右手剪刀：剪不好不是手笨，是工具不配。

concepts.def: Organises four culture orientations along internal–external focus and flexibility–stability/control axes.
concepts.defZh: Quinn & Rohrbaugh（1983）：Clan/Involvement、Adhocracy/Adaptability、Hierarchy/Consistency、Market/Achievement；不是发展阶段。
concepts.one: 用内外关注和灵活或稳定两条轴，把文化分成四种取向，没有哪种普遍最好。
concepts.eg: Apex 看重外部业绩指标，是成就型；医院靠清楚流程可靠运作，是一致性型。
concepts.like: 像坐标图的四个象限：先看横轴竖轴，再定组织落在哪一格。

concepts.def: External focus plus stability/control: competitiveness, clear targets and measurable results, possibly with autonomy over methods.
concepts.defZh: 例：Apex Sales Group；有自主选方法不等于适应型；稳定/控制指结果控制，不证明外部稳定。
concepts.one: 成就取向是外部关注加稳定控制：重视竞争力、明确目标和可衡量的结果。
concepts.eg: Apex 设有挑战性的指标、每月复盘，晋升紧扣业绩，但具体怎么做由员工自己选。
concepts.like: 像按终点成绩排名的比赛：怎么跑你自己定，最后只看名次。

concepts.def: A diagnostic that separately checks whether performance goals are achieved and whether values are practised.
concepts.defZh: 四象限组织调查而非人格标签或人事处方；高结果低价值要问结果如何取得、需复核哪些风险。
concepts.one: 把目标是否达成和价值是否践行分开检查，组成四个象限来诊断问题。
concepts.eg: 销售员超额完成指标，却是靠隐瞒客户信息、排挤同事做到的，要追问结果是怎么来的。
concepts.like: 像比赛既看得分也看犯规：跑得快却越出赛道，成绩也要复核。

tf.q: In Schein's model, basic underlying assumptions are the most visible level of culture.
tf.exp: 最可见的是可见表征（artifacts）；基本假设是最深的一层，习以为常，很少被说出来。

tf.q: Holding regular open meetings is sufficient evidence that employees feel safe to express disagreement.
tf.exp: 开会只是一种可见表征，看得见却不好解读；员工敢不敢说，要看实际决策和他们的经历。

tf.q: A gap between stated values and practised values automatically proves that everyone in the organisation is hypocritical.
tf.exp: 差距不一定是虚伪，可能来自相互冲突的要求、部门差异或价值尚未落实，要先查它在哪里发生。

tf.q: Built to Last compared 18 visionary companies with 18 comparison companies using historical material.
tf.exp: Collins 和 Porras（1994）做的是历史比较，不能据此说文化是成功唯一原因。

tf.q: The "clock building" idea means organisations should build capabilities and mechanisms that do not depend on a single charismatic leader.
tf.exp: 造钟是建立职责、程序、接班安排和共享价值，让组织不靠某一个人；报时则只靠领导个人魅力。

tf.q: "Preserve the core, stimulate progress" means an organisation should protect all of its existing routines and practices.
tf.exp: 要守住的只是核心理念，具体做法应该不断更新；把所有熟悉的老惯例都当成核心就错了。

tf.q: Culture strength includes both consensus (how widely expectations are shared) and intensity (how strongly they are held and reinforced).
tf.exp: Chatman 和 O'Reilly（2016）的文化强度就含这两个成分，和文化内容不同。

tf.q: A strong culture is, by definition, a good culture that will produce higher performance.
tf.exp: 强度和内容要分开评价。文化强只说明大家一致，内容可能并不适合任务或环境，所以强不等于好。

tf.q: Sørensen (2002) found that the performance-reliability advantage of strong cultures disappeared in volatile environments.
tf.exp: 稳定环境里强文化和更可靠的绩效相关，波动环境里这个优势消失；是优势消失，不是必然下降。

tf.q: A single company event can contain several visible forms of culture at once, such as a ritual, slogan, hero and symbol.
tf.exp: 一场年度颁奖礼就能同时包含仪式、口号、英雄和象征物；分类是用来识别信息的，不是唯一标签。

tf.q: Hofstede's national-culture dimensions can be used to reliably predict an individual employee's behaviour.
tf.exp: 维度说的是国家层面的大体倾向，不是固定规则；国家文化推不出个人行为，也不等于组织文化。

tf.q: In Stephens et al. (2012), "first-generation students" refers to students whose parents did not attend university.
tf.exp: 第一代大学生指父母没上过大学的学生，不是第一代移民；这项研究的情境是美国大学。

tf.q: The cultural mismatch research shows that all first-generation students are interdependent and less capable.
tf.exp: 研究不能这样推论：困难来自制度规范和个人背景的互动，有差异不等于能力不足。

tf.q: In the Competing Values Framework, the Hierarchy (Consistency) orientation combines an internal focus with stability and control.
tf.exp: 一致性型就是内部关注加稳定控制，重视协调、清楚的程序和可靠运作。

tf.q: The four CVF orientations represent developmental stages that organisations pass through in order.
tf.exp: 四种取向不是组织依次经过的发展阶段，也不由规模或行业直接决定；没有哪一种普遍最优。

mcq.q: A firm's mission statement emphasises openness, it holds monthly town-hall meetings, but employees privately believe that questioning a manager will harm their careers. The private belief is an example of:
mcq.exp: 员工私下默认「质疑经理会受损」，是没人说出口却支配行动的基本深层假设。开会是可见表征，使命里的开放是宣称的价值。

mcq.q: Which evidence would best reveal an organisation's practised values rather than its stated values?
options: The values listed on its website
Who gets recognised and how decisions are made when priorities conflict
The CEO's speech at the annual conference
The wording of its mission statement
mcq.exp: 践行的价值藏在实际行动里：谁被表彰、优先级冲突时怎么决定。官网、使命和讲话都只是宣称的价值。

mcq.q: Before founding Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo, Masaru Ibuka's lab developed a rice cooker that cooked rice unevenly and failed. Built to Last uses such cases to challenge which myth?
options: Great companies must start with a great initial idea or product
Great companies require a charismatic leader
Profit maximisation must be the main purpose
mcq.exp: 这是在打破「伟大公司必须始于绝妙产品」的误区：长期成功靠的是持续学习和抓住后续机会，好产品仍然重要。

mcq.q: A founder personally makes every key decision, and the company struggles after he retires because no routines or successors were developed. In Built to Last terms, he was:
mcq.exp: 一切靠创始人个人的知识和魅力，他走了公司就转不动，这就是报时；造钟则是留下不依赖某个人的机制。

mcq.q: A university keeps its commitment to high-quality education but moves from face-to-face classes to blended learning and updates its assessments. This best illustrates:
mcq.exp: 大学守住了高质量教育这个核心承诺，只是更新了教学和考核方式，这正是保留核心、推动进步，不是放弃理念。

mcq.q: Two organisations are both highly unified: one firmly supports experimenting with new methods, the other firmly requires following procedures to avoid errors. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Only the experimenting organisation has a strong culture
Both may be strong cultures but differ in culture content
Both have weak cultures because they differ
Both will necessarily perform equally well
mcq.exp: 文化强度看共识和强度，文化内容看鼓励什么；两家都高度一致，都可能是强文化，只是鼓励的工作方式不同。

mcq.q: Most members of a team agree that work should be checked before submission, and they actively remind and pressure each other to comply. This combination describes:
mcq.exp: 大多数人都认同，这是高共识；大家认真执行还互相提醒和施压，这种社会强化就是高强度。

mcq.q: A firm with a very strong culture has operated in a stable market for decades, but the market has suddenly become volatile. Based on Sørensen (2002), what is the most accurate expectation?
options: Its strong culture will guarantee the highest profits
Its strong culture will necessarily cause performance to decline
The performance-reliability advantage of its strong culture may disappear, so managers should check whether shared expectations still fit
Culture strength has no relationship with performance in any environment
mcq.exp: 强文化的可靠性优势在波动环境里会消失，所以要检查共享期待是否还合适；不能说成必然下降，可靠也不等于高利润。

mcq.q: Walmart employees repeatedly perform a cheer that spells out the company name and emphasises customers first. This is best classified as a:
mcq.exp: 员工反复一起参与、借此表达共同意义，这就是仪式；但这证明不了每位员工都喜欢它或因此更投入。

mcq.q: Nordstrom's inverted pyramid places customers at the top and managers at the bottom. What should an analyst check before concluding that it reflects the actual culture?
options: Whether frontline staff actually have the authority, resources and management support to solve customer problems
Whether the pyramid is printed in the annual report
Whether formal authority has been abolished
mcq.exp: 倒金字塔只是表达意图的象征物，要核实一线员工是否真有权限、资源和管理层支持；它也不代表正式权威被取消了。

mcq.q: A manager learns that her new team comes from a country with high uncertainty avoidance. The most appropriate use of Hofstede's framework is to:
options: Assume every team member wants strict rules
Assume the organisation's culture matches the national culture
Use the dimension to ask team members what rules and information they need, then observe
mcq.exp: 正确用法是把维度当提问的线索：先问大家需要什么规则和信息，再观察实际行为。国家层面的倾向不是个人定律。

mcq.q: In a team introduction, one member describes her personal skills and interests, while another describes his role in the team and his working relationships. These reflect, respectively:
mcq.exp: 先讲个人技能和兴趣的是独立自我，先讲团队角色和工作关系的是互依自我；这只是当下的表现，不能给人永久贴标签。

mcq.q: A company frequently gives awards only to individual top performers. An employee who values shared team contributions feels that the team's support goes unrecognised. This is best explained as:
mcq.exp: 公司只表彰个人，这是独立取向的期待；员工看重团队共同贡献，是互依取向。两者对不上就是文化错配，不是他能力不足。

mcq.q: BrightWave Digital tracks customer trends and new technologies, encourages experimentation and rapid prototyping, and supports trying new approaches when the market changes. Its dominant orientation is:
mcq.exp: 追踪市场和新技术、鼓励实验和快速试做，这是外部关注加灵活性，也就是适应型（Adhocracy）。

mcq.q: Apex Sales Group sets challenging targets, reviews results monthly, lets employees choose their own methods, and ties promotion closely to measurable performance. Why is it classified as Achievement rather than Adaptability?
options: Because employees have autonomy over methods
Because its dominant priority is external, measurable results and competitiveness
Because it has rigid process controls
Because it focuses on internal teamwork
mcq.exp: 分类看的是主导优先事项：Apex 最看重外部的、可衡量的业绩和竞争力，所以是成就型。让员工自选方法不等于就是适应型。

mcq.q: Central Health Services has clear procedures for medication, records and patient handovers, defined roles, and supervisors who check compliance. Which CVF quadrant applies?
mcq.exp: 程序清楚、角色明确、主管检查合规，这是内部关注加稳定控制，也就是一致性型；但它不只是僵化的官僚，重点是可靠运作。

mcq.q: A salesperson exceeds every target but does so by withholding information from customers and undermining colleagues. On the values–performance matrix, the manager should first ask:
options: What capabilities are missing and what resources need improving?
How were the results obtained and what risks need review?
Which practices support both and can they be sustained?
Nothing, because the targets were met
mcq.exp: 目标达成了但价值被忽视，这个象限要先问结果是怎么来的、有哪些风险要复核；业绩再高也不能容忍违规。

mcq.q: A team says it values collaboration but rarely shares information. The manager listens to staff experiences, clarifies expectations for sharing, schedules joint time and adjusts recognition, then reviews collaboration and delivery. This sequence follows:
mcq.exp: 这是管理文化的四步：先诊断实际行为，再澄清期待，然后对齐领导和资源，最后评估并调整；它不保证一次就建成理想文化。

match.title: Match each Competing Values Framework orientation to its axes and priorities
pairs: External focus + flexibility: learning, experimentation, responding to change
External focus + stability/control: results, competitiveness, accountability
Internal focus + flexibility: participation, teamwork, member development
Internal focus + stability/control: coordination, procedures, reliability

match.title: Match each visible form of culture to its example or feature
pairs: Walmart employees repeatedly performing the company cheer
A planned annual event publicly recognising cross-department collaboration
A repeatedly told story of an employee who went out of her way to help a customer
Nordstrom's inverted pyramid with customers at the top

essay.q: Case: Lumen Tech's website states that "openness and employee wellbeing" are its core values, and it holds a monthly open forum. However, last year an engineer who raised concerns about unrealistic deadlines at the forum was later passed over for a key project. Since then, staff rarely speak at forums, and requests to reduce excessive workloads are routinely declined. The CEO is puzzled and plans to run a values workshop. Using Schein's levels of culture and the distinction between stated and practised values, diagnose the situation and recommend what management should do.
points: Artifacts: monthly open forum; espoused values: openness and wellbeing on the website
Basic underlying assumption: speaking up carries career costs (learned from the engineer's experience)
Gap between stated and practised values: decisions, recognition and workload responses contradict the stated values
Culture is learned through shared experience; one workshop cannot replace changing actual practice
Recommend: diagnose experiences, clarify that reasonable dissent will not be punished, align opportunity allocation and workload decisions, evaluate whether concerns are raised and handled
Avoid concluding everyone is hypocritical; investigate where and why the gap occurs
essay.model: Schein distinguishes three levels of culture. At Lumen Tech the monthly forum is an artifact and the website's commitment to openness and wellbeing is an espoused value. However, culture is learned through shared experience: when the engineer who raised concerns was passed over, employees learned that speaking up carries career costs. This has likely become a basic underlying assumption – a taken-for-granted belief that now guides behaviour, explaining why forums are silent. The case also shows a gap between stated and practised values. Practised values are visible in decisions, recognition and what behaviour is accepted or corrected; here, opportunity allocation and the routine refusal of workload requests contradict the stated values. The forum's existence cannot prove openness, because artifacts are easy to observe but hard to interpret. A values workshop alone is unlikely to work, because it repeats the espoused level without changing practice. Management should follow a diagnose–clarify–align–evaluate sequence: listen to employees' experiences and examine how project and workload decisions are made; clarify that reasonable dissent will not be penalised; align leaders' actions, project allocation and workload resources with the stated values; and evaluate over time whether concerns are raised and handled seriously. Management should also avoid assuming everyone is hypocritical, since the gap may come from competing demands or particular units.

essay.q: Case: Harbour Logistics has had a very strong culture for 30 years: almost all staff share and firmly enforce the belief that "we always follow the established process exactly". This produced highly reliable delivery performance in a stable market. In the past two years, customer demands and technology have changed rapidly, competitors have introduced flexible services, and Harbour's performance has become uneven. A new manager argues that "a strong culture is always an advantage, so we should just reinforce it". Evaluate this argument using concepts from this week.
points: Define culture strength as consensus plus intensity; Harbour scores high on both
Distinguish strength from content: the content (strict process adherence) may not fit the new environment
Sørensen (2002): strong cultures linked to reliable performance in stable environments, advantage disappears in volatile ones; association not causal law
Built to Last: preserve the core, stimulate progress – separate core commitments from familiar routines
CVF: current Consistency (Hierarchy) emphasis may need more Adaptability (external + flexibility) practices
Recommend diagnosing which expectations still fit, and aligning recognition and resources with needed behaviours
essay.model: The manager's argument confuses culture strength with culture content. Following Chatman and O'Reilly (2016), strength combines consensus – how widely an expectation is shared – and intensity – how strongly it is held and socially reinforced. Harbour is high on both, but strength says nothing about whether the content, strict adherence to established process, suits the current task and environment. Sørensen (2002) found that strong cultures were associated with more reliable performance in relatively stable environments, but this advantage disappeared in volatile environments. Harbour's history fits the first condition and its recent uneven results are consistent with the second, although this is an association rather than proof that strong culture causes decline. Simply reinforcing old habits therefore risks locking in behaviour that no longer fits. In Competing Values terms, Harbour has a Consistency (Hierarchy) emphasis – internal focus and stability/control – while the new environment demands more Adaptability: attention to external signals, experimentation and changed practice. Built to Last's principle of preserving the core while stimulating progress is useful: management should identify the genuine core commitment, such as reliable service to customers, and separate it from familiar routines that can be updated. Management should diagnose which shared expectations still fit, clarify the new behaviours needed, align recognition and resources to support experimentation, and evaluate results over time.

essay.q: Case: Westbridge University's student support centre has a strongly service-minded team: staff treat students respectfully and help each other, but average waiting times have exceeded targets for three consecutive months. Meanwhile, the university's orientation messaging stresses "be independent, find your own path and speak up for yourself", and staff notice that some first-generation students rarely use the centre and report feeling out of place. The director plans to run more value-awareness sessions. Using the values–performance matrix and the concept of cultural mismatch, analyse the situation and recommend actions.
points: Matrix: values practised but goals not achieved – ask what capabilities are missing and what resources need improving
Do not assume staff lack commitment to service; investigate skills, workload, systems and resources
Value-awareness sessions alone do not change practice; clarify waiting-time targets and trial targeted improvements
Cultural mismatch: independence-focused norms may mismatch the interdependent orientation of some first-generation students (Stephens et al. 2012)
Avoid generalising: not all first-generation students are interdependent or less capable; mismatch arises from institution–background interaction
Inclusive culture: recognise differences, create multiple ways to participate, align practices (e.g. framing support around community)
essay.model: The values–performance matrix separates whether performance goals are achieved from whether values are practised. The support team falls in the 'values practised, goals not achieved' quadrant, so the right questions are what capabilities are missing and what resources need improving. Respectful, helpful behaviour shows the team already practises its service values, so more value-awareness sessions are unlikely to reduce waiting times. The director should clarify the waiting-time target, investigate skills, workload, booking systems and staffing, trial a targeted improvement, and then review service behaviour and waiting times separately. The second issue concerns cultural mismatch. Stephens et al. (2012) showed that in US universities, norms emphasising independence can mismatch the interdependent orientation of some first-generation students – those whose parents did not attend university – leading to discomfort, tasks feeling harder and poorer performance; framing the university around interdependence was linked to better task performance. Westbridge's 'be independent' messaging may make some students feel help-seeking does not belong to them. The director should not assume all first-generation students are interdependent or less capable, since mismatch arises from the interaction between institutional norms and background. Building an inclusive culture means recognising differences, creating varied ways to participate, such as peer or group-based support, and aligning messaging with inclusive values, then checking whether usage and student experiences actually change.
